QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_27

question.text: Per SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018, a 'Social Impact Assessor' is defined as an individual who:

answer.text: Holds a SEBI registration as a Research Analyst and has completed a 40-hour CSR compliance programme.

Is registered with a self-regulatory organisation under the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (or such other agency as may be specified by SEBI), has qualified the NISM certification programme, and holds a valid certificate.
Is employed by the issuing NPO with at least 3 years of tenure.
Is a practicing Chartered Accountant for at least 10 years, regardless of NISM certification.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p.57 of the workbook, the ICDR definition of 'social impact assessor' is an individual registered with a self-regulatory organisation under ICAI (or other SEBI-specified agency) who has qualified the NISM certification programme and holds a valid certificate. Per p.59, the SRO is the 'Institute of Social Auditors of India' under ICAI. The Trap: Option A confuses the RA registration regime. Option C violates the independence requirement — the SIA must be independent from the SE. Option D bypasses the NISM certification requirement. Note: Eligibility rests on three legs: SRO registration under ICAI, NISM qualification, and a valid certificate. All three are stated on pp.57 and 59 of the workbook.
